issues.title: Stop overlapping bookings of different lengths, at the write
issues.description:
## Context
- Repository: `/work/booking` (git). Work on branch `fix/overlap`. Base: `main` at `1d8db4b`.
- App: `app/` is a Cloudflare Worker with a D1 database (D1 is SQLite). Booking logic lives in `app/src/booking.js` (`createBooking`). Schema: `app/migrations/0001_init.sql`.
- Commit `259df74` on this branch adds `app/tests/overlap.test.js`, which fails today. This is a seeded exercise: the defect was planted on purpose for this rehearsal, and the test was written before any fix.

## Problem
`createBooking` only refuses a booking that starts at exactly the same instant as a confirmed one, and it reads before it writes. So sessions of different lengths can overlap (60 min at 08:00 and 30 min at 08:30), and two simultaneous requests can both pass the read.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Overlapping confirmed sessions for the same teacher in the same sandbox are impossible, for any mix of 30, 45 and 60 minutes. Adjacent sessions (one ends when the next starts) stay allowed.
2. The guarantee holds at the database write, not only in an earlier read: concurrent requests confirm at most one. D1 is SQLite, so there are no exclusion constraints. Any schema change must stay backwards compatible: the previous release must still run against the new schema, because a rollback is part of this release.
3. A retry with the same idempotency key still returns the original booking (HTTP 200), also under concurrency.
4. Cancelled sessions never block a new booking.
5. `cd app && npm test` passes. Do not weaken or delete existing tests.

## Constraints
- Do not push and do not deploy. Commit on `fix/overlap` only.
- Keep the change small. No new dependencies.

## Next action
Implementer: make the change, commit, comment with the SHA and the test summary, then set the issue to done (it goes to review, then to the operator for approval).

comments.body:
## Done — overlap is now refused by the INSERT itself

Commit: `13e6509` (`13e650970474c7b98270d233efee21b9288a3db2`) on `fix/overlap`. Not pushed, not deployed.

**What changed** — `app/src/booking.js` only. The pre-write `start_utc = ?` SELECT is gone; `createBooking` now writes through one conditional statement:

```sql
INSERT INTO bookings (...) SELECT ?, ?, ...
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bookings WHERE sandbox = ? AND teacher_id = ?
  AND status = 'confirmed' AND start_utc < ? AND end_utc > ?)
```

**Why this shape**

- `start_utc < newEnd AND end_utc > newStart` is the half-open interval test, so any mix of 30/45/60 conflicts when it really overlaps and adjacent sessions (one ends as the next starts) still fit.
- The test sits *inside* the write. SQLite, and so D1, runs a single statement in its own transaction holding the write lock, so nothing can slip a row in between the test and the insert — that gap is exactly what let two concurrent requests both confirm. `meta.changes === 0` means the interval was taken.
- On `0` rows written I look up the idempotency key first: a concurrent retry of the same request gets its original booking back with **200**, anything else gets **409 slot_taken**. The `UNIQUE (sandbox, idem_key)` catch now also maps a reused key to **422** instead of leaking a raw constraint error.
- `status = 'confirmed'` in the guard, so cancelled sessions never block.
- **No schema change at all**, which makes the rollback requirement trivial: the previous release runs against an untouched `0001_init.sql`. No new dependencies; net +35/−13 lines in one file.

**Tests** — `cd app && npm test`: **22 pass, 0 fail** (80 ms). The five `overlap.test.js` tests that failed on the baseline now pass; the 17 pre-existing tests are untouched and still green. Baseline before the change was 17 pass / 5 fail.

Beyond the suite I ran a throwaway sweep (outside the repo, not committed) to check the invariant rather than just the examples:

- all 81 sequential combinations of (60/45/30) × (60/45/30) × offsets −60…+60 min — conflict exactly when the intervals overlap, no false 409s on adjacent starts;
- 200 rounds of 12 mutually overlapping concurrent requests — never two confirmed bookings that overlap, every loser a clean 409, confirmed count always equal to the number of fulfilled calls;
- 200 rounds of 8 concurrent requests sharing one idempotency key — always exactly one row and one booking id, zero rejections;
- cancel-then-rebook-overlapping, repeated. All clean.

**Worth a reviewer's eye**

- I deliberately chose the conditional INSERT over the alternative (a `booking_slots` table with `UNIQUE (sandbox, teacher_id, slot)` filled in the same `db.batch` transaction). The slot table would make the invariant a hard DB constraint that even buggy code cannot violate, but it needs a migration, cancel-path slot cleanup, and it interacts awkwardly with the rollback requirement — the previous release would write bookings without slot rows, so the constraint would protect nothing after a rollback anyway. The conditional INSERT satisfies criterion 2 with no schema change. Happy to switch if you want the constraint to be structural.
- The guarantee relies on D1 running one statement atomically with `meta.changes` reported accurately. If `meta.changes` were ever absent, my `?? 0` fallback degrades to the idempotency lookup, which returns the booking that was just written as a 200 replay — a wrong status code in that hypothetical, never a lost or duplicated booking.
- The existing index `(sandbox, teacher_id, status, start_utc)` serves the new range predicate; I did not add one.

## Approved — every criterion met, verified independently

Reviewed `1d8db4b..13e6509` on `fix/overlap`. Diff is two files: `app/src/booking.js` (+35/−13) and the new `app/tests/overlap.test.js`. I confirmed `app/migrations/0001_init.sql`, `app/src/worker.js`, `app/src/time.js`, the three pre-existing test files, `app/tests/helpers.js`, `app/tests/d1-sqlite.js`, `app/package.json`, `app/wrangler.toml`, `scripts/` and `.github/workflows/` are byte-for-byte untouched, and the working tree is clean. Nothing unrelated changed; no existing test was weakened or deleted.

### Evidence per criterion

**1. No overlap for any mix of 30/45/60; adjacent still allowed.**
`app/src/booking.js:103-104` uses the half-open predicate `start_utc < :newEnd AND end_utc > :newStart`. I did not take the five seeded cases as proof — I ran my own exhaustive sequential sweep of all 81 combinations (60/45/60 × 30/45/60 × offsets −60…+60 at 15-min steps, the full availability window): the create call was refused with 409 in exactly the cases where the intervals truly intersect, accepted in every other, and no pair of confirmed rows ever overlapped. Adjacency (`end == start`) is accepted, matching the pre-existing `adjacent sessions do not conflict (end is exclusive)` test, which still passes.

**2. The guarantee is at the write, and the rollback is safe.**
The pre-write `start_utc = ?` SELECT is gone (removed at the old `createBooking` clash block); the only gate is now inside the statement that writes — `INSERT … SELECT ? … WHERE NOT EXISTS (…)` in `insertIfFree` (`app/src/booking.js:98-110`), with `meta.changes === 0` as the "interval taken" signal. One SQLite statement runs in its own implicit transaction under the write lock, so there is no read-then-write window left to lose. 300 rounds of 12 mutually overlapping concurrent `createBooking` calls on the real `node:sqlite`-backed D1 stand-in: zero overlapping confirmed rows, every loser a clean `409 slot_taken` (no raw SQL errors leaking), and the confirmed-row count equal to the fulfilled-call count every round — so the winner is never lost either.
Schema diff is empty. `0001_init.sql` is unchanged, which is strictly stronger than backwards compatible: the previous release runs against the identical schema, so the rollback in this release carries no migration risk. The existing index `(sandbox, teacher_id, status, start_utc)` already covers the new range predicate.

**3. Idempotent retry returns the original, also under concurrency.**
Two paths are covered and both are reachable. Same-key retry at the *same* interval: the second insert writes 0 rows (its own row now blocks it), falls to `findByKey` + `sameRequest` at `app/src/booking.js:144-145` and returns 200 replayed. Same-key at a *non-overlapping* interval: the `UNIQUE (sandbox, idem_key)` violation is caught at `:134-137` and mapped to `422 idempotency_key_reused` instead of leaking the constraint error. 300 rounds of 8 concurrent calls sharing one key: always exactly one confirmed row, one booking id, exactly one 201 and seven 200s, zero rejections.

**4. Cancelled sessions never block.**
`status = 'confirmed'` is in the `NOT EXISTS` guard (`app/src/booking.js:103`). 50 rounds of cancel-then-rebook-overlapping across all three durations: every rebook returned 201 and left exactly one confirmed row. The pre-existing `cancellation frees the slot and is idempotent` test still passes.

**5. Tests.**
`cd app && npm test` run by me: **22 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped** (71 ms). The 17 pre-existing tests are all green and unmodified; the 5 new `overlap.test.js` tests cover the reported defect directly.

### One non-blocking note (no change required)

Concurrent same-key misuse where the two requests *overlap* — key `K` for 08:00/60 racing `K` for 08:30/30 — returns `409 slot_taken` rather than the `422 idempotency_key_reused` the sequential path gives, because `written === 0` is reached before the UNIQUE violation can fire (`app/src/booking.js:141-146`). I verified this: non-overlapping gives 422, overlapping gives 409. Both are honest about the outcome, exactly one row is written either way, and no criterion covers it. Worth a line of follow-up only if the API contract wants one status for key reuse regardless of timing.

I agree with the implementer's call to skip the `booking_slots` table: a structural constraint that the rolled-back release would not populate protects nothing after the rollback, and criterion 2 is already satisfied at the write without a migration.

Moving to the approval stage for the operator. Still unpushed and undeployed, as the constraints require.

Operator decision: approve 13e6509 for release.

What I inspected before deciding:
- The diff 259df74..13e6509: one file, app/src/booking.js. The pre-write SELECT is gone; the overlap test is inside the INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS, half-open interval, confirmed rows only. No schema change.
- `npm test` on a fresh checkout of the exported commit: 22 pass, 0 fail.
- Against a local D1 (wrangler dev, real SQLite): 5 rounds of three overlapping requests (60, 30 and 45 minutes) sent at the same instant, each round in a fresh sandbox: 201/409/409 every time, one confirmed booking per round.
- Same script against the current staging release (37d56fd, without the fix): 3 of 3 rounds confirmed all three, so the test does detect the defect.
- The reviewer note on concurrent same-key misuse (409 instead of 422 when the intervals overlap) is accepted as is: one row is written either way.

Next: this closes the Paperclip side. Release goes through the separate path: pull request, CI, merge, staging, then the protected production environment, which needs its own approval for this exact commit.

issues.title: Pin the slot list around the Paris clock change (25 Oct 2026)
issues.description:
## Context
- Repository: `/work/booking` (git). Create branch `test/clock-change` from `fix/overlap` (HEAD `13e6509`, which was approved in BOO-1).
- Slot listing lives in `app/src/booking.js` (`listSlots`); time helpers in `app/src/time.js`; existing time tests in `app/tests/time.test.js`.

## Problem
Paris leaves summer time on Sunday 25 October 2026 while Sydney stays on summer time. The gap between the teacher (Paris) and the learner (Sydney) changes from 9 to 10 hours. There is one test for this today; the slot list for a whole day on each side of the change is not pinned.

## Acceptance criteria
1. New tests show, for a 45-minute session, the full list of start times on Saturday 24 October and on Monday 26 October 2026 (Sydney dates), with both the Sydney and the Paris time of each slot.
2. A booking made for the first slot of Monday 26 October is stored as the correct UTC instant.
3. `cd app && npm test` passes. Only test files change.

## Constraints
- Do not push or deploy. Commit on `test/clock-change` only. No new dependencies.

## Next action
Implementer: write the tests, run them, commit, comment with the SHA and the test summary, then set the issue to done.

comments.body:
## Done

Added `app/tests/clock-change.test.js`, pinning the 45-minute slot list on each side of the Paris clock change (Sun 25 Oct 2026). Paris leaves summer time while Sydney stays on it, so the teacher/learner gap grows from 9 to 10 hours. Only one test covered this before; a whole day's slot list on either side was unpinned.

**What the tests assert**

- The full Saturday 24 Oct 2026 list (Sydney date) as `[UTC instant, Sydney wall clock, Paris wall clock]` — 7 starts, 05:00Z–08:00Z, Paris 07:00–10:00, Sydney 16:00–19:00.
- The full Monday 26 Oct 2026 list — same 7 starts in Paris terms, but 06:00Z–09:00Z and Sydney 17:00–20:00.
- The Paris day keeps its shape across the change while every Sydney start moves exactly one hour later, so a regression shows up as a list diff rather than one changed field.
- Booking the first slot of Mon 26 Oct stores `2026-10-26T06:00:00.000Z` / end `06:45:00.000Z` — the post-change instant, not the `05:00Z` summer time would give. Checked on the presented booking *and* by reading `start_utc`/`end_utc` off the stored row, so this pins the instant rather than a wall-clock string.
- Offsets are asserted directly: Paris 120 → 60 min, Sydney 660 both days.

**One thing worth flagging for review**

The interrupted earlier run had left this file expecting only the first slot of Mon 26 Oct to be taken after booking it. That expectation was wrong and it was the single failing test. Starts are 30 minutes apart but the session runs 45, so a booking at 07:00 Paris also covers the 07:30 start — both come back `taken`. I verified that against `listSlots` directly and corrected the test to pin the real behaviour (two taken, five free) with a comment saying why. The app was right; no source change was needed.

**Test summary** — `cd app && npm test`: **26 tests, 26 pass, 0 fail** (~98 ms). Test files only; `git diff --stat fix/overlap` shows no source changes.

- Commit: `2dfd1b3` on `test/clock-change`
- Not pushed, not deployed.

## Approved

Reviewed `2dfd1b3` on `test/clock-change` against `fix/overlap` (`13e6509`). Diff is one new file, `app/tests/clock-change.test.js`, +98 lines — no source, migration, or config change, so nothing to roll back and no schema risk.

**Evidence per criterion**

1. **Full slot list on both sides, Sydney and Paris times** — met. Each test pins all 7 starts for a 45-minute session as `[UTC instant, Sydney label, Paris label]`:
   - Sat 24 Oct (Sydney date): `05:00Z`–`08:00Z`, Paris 07:00–10:00 (CEST, +2), Sydney 16:00–19:00.
   - Mon 26 Oct: `06:00Z`–`09:00Z`, Paris 07:00–10:00 (CET, +1), Sydney 17:00–20:00.
   I recomputed both lists independently of the app (plain `Intl` in a scratch script) and they match exactly, so the expectations are correct values, not transcribed output. 7 starts is also right: the teacher window is 07:00–11:00 Paris with 30-minute steps, and a 10:30 start would end 11:15, past the edge. Offsets are asserted directly (Paris 120 → 60, Sydney 660 both days), which is what makes a tzdata or offset regression fail loudly.
2. **Booking the first Monday slot stores the correct instant** — met, and checked at the write, not just the read: the test asserts the presented booking (`2026-10-26T06:00:00.000Z` / `06:45:00.000Z`) **and** then reads `start_utc`/`end_utc` off the stored row via `SELECT … WHERE id = ?`, comparing to `Date.parse(...)`. `06:00Z` is the post-change instant; summer time would have given `05:00Z`. Validation on that path is real too — `withinAvailability` re-derives the Paris wall clock from the instant, so a wrong instant would have been rejected rather than silently stored.
3. **Suite passes, test files only** — met. I ran `cd app && npm test` myself: **26 tests, 26 pass, 0 fail** (77 ms), including the 10 pre-existing booking/overlap/idempotency/cancellation tests and the 6 time tests. `git diff --stat fix/overlap...test/clock-change` → `1 file changed, 98 insertions(+)`. Working tree clean; no remote configured, so nothing was pushed, and no deploy.

**On the flagged expectation change**

The implementer's correction is right, and I verified it against the code rather than the summary. The booking covers `06:00Z`–`06:45Z`; the next start is `06:30Z`–`07:15Z`, and `listSlots` marks a start taken when `b.start_utc < e && b.end_utc > s`, so `06:30Z` overlaps and both come back `taken` while `07:00Z` onward stay free. Two taken / five free is the real behaviour, and the comment in the test explains why — correct to pin that rather than change the app.

**Other things I checked**

- Concurrency and idempotency are untouched by this change; the single-statement `INSERT … WHERE NOT EXISTS` guard and the retry/`UNIQUE` replay paths in `createBooking` still pass their existing tests.
- Each test calls `fresh()` for its own DB and `req()` mints a unique idempotency key, so the new file cannot leak state into or out of the rest of the suite.
- The tests are non-vacuous: `deepEqual` against fixed 7-element arrays fails on any shift in instant, label, or list length — an empty or one-hour-off list cannot pass.

One minor, non-blocking note for later: the assertions depend on the `en-AU` label format (`'Mon, 26 Oct, 17:00'`), so an ICU formatting change in a future Node could break these alongside the existing tests that already use those labels. Not a reason to hold this.

Operator decision: approve 2dfd1b3 (tests only).

What I inspected:
- Diff 13e6509..2dfd1b3: one new file, app/tests/clock-change.test.js, no source change.
- `npm test` on a fresh checkout of the exported commit: 26 pass, 0 fail.
- The expectation the retried run corrected (a 45-minute booking at 07:00 Paris also blocks the 07:30 start) matches the overlap rule approved in BOO-1.

Not merged into the released branch during this rehearsal, so the production commit stays fixed; it is pushed as its own branch with a pull request.

issues.title: Replays survive the cutoff; the sandbox limit holds at the write
issues.description:
## Context
- Repository: `/work/booking` (git). Work on branch `fix/replay-and-limit`. Base: `main` at `e85cdb8` (a local `main` branch exists for diffs).
- Booking logic: `app/src/booking.js` (`validateRequest`, `createBooking`, `insertIfFree`).
- Commit `143ee46` adds `app/tests/replay-and-limit.test.js`, which fails today on 3 of its 4 cases. These are real defects found by an external review of the demo, not seeded ones.

## Problem
1. `createBooking` runs the moving eligibility rules (at least one hour ahead, within 28 days, inside availability) before it looks up the idempotency key. A retry of a booking that already succeeded fails with 422 `too_soon` once the cutoff passes.
2. The per-sandbox limit (40 confirmed bookings) is a separate read before the insert, so concurrent requests can push a sandbox past it.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Split validation: structural checks (sandbox, key, duration, instant with an offset, 15-minute boundary, time zone) run first; the idempotency lookup comes next; eligibility rules apply only when a new booking is created.
2. A replay with the same key and payload returns the original booking with 200, even after the cutoff, and even if it was cancelled (it stays cancelled). The same key with a different payload is still 422 `idempotency_key_reused`.
3. The limit holds at the write, in the same statement as the overlap check: concurrent requests never leave more than 40 confirmed bookings in a sandbox; the refused ones get 429 `sandbox_full`; an overlap still gets 409.
4. No schema change. `cd app && npm test` passes; do not weaken or delete existing tests.

## Constraints
- Do not push or deploy. Commit on `fix/replay-and-limit` only. No new dependencies.

## Next action
Implementer: make the change, commit, comment with the SHA and the test summary, then set the issue to done.

comments.body:
## Done

Split validation so a replay never re-runs the moving rules, and moved the per-sandbox limit into the write.

**What changed** (`app/src/booking.js`, no schema change)

- `validateRequest` is now two functions. `validateStructure` checks the shape of the request — sandbox, idempotency key, duration, an instant with an offset, the 15-minute boundary, the time zone — and `checkEligibility` holds the rules that move with the clock: at least one hour ahead, within 28 days, inside availability.
- `createBooking` runs the structural checks, then the idempotency lookup, then `checkEligibility` only when it is about to create a new booking. A replay with the same key and payload returns the original booking with 200 however late the retry arrives, and a cancelled booking stays cancelled. The same key with a different payload is still 422 `idempotency_key_reused`.
- The confirmed-booking count moved into the `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE` alongside the overlap test, so one statement under SQLite's write lock decides both. The separate `SELECT COUNT(*)` before the insert is gone — that read was what concurrent requests could overtake.
- A write that finds no room is diagnosed afterwards by the new `refusal` helper: an overlap is 409 `slot_taken`, a full sandbox is 429 `sandbox_full`. A concurrent retry of the same key still replays with 200 before either is considered.

**Why:** the eligibility rules answer a different question from "is this request well formed". Their answers change as time passes, so running them ahead of the idempotency lookup made a successful booking un-replayable once its cutoff went by. The limit had the same shape of bug as the overlap check did before it: a read that another request can get between.

**Commit:** `f62a312737e18782d7a2834e983da6d66cbea81f` on `fix/replay-and-limit` (not pushed).

**Tests:** `cd app && npm test` → **34 pass, 0 fail**. All four cases in `app/tests/replay-and-limit.test.js` pass (3 failed before). No existing test was changed, weakened or removed.

I also checked by hand, outside the suite: a fresh key in a full sandbox gets 429, a replay in a full sandbox still returns 200, an overlap in a full sandbox gets 409, and after one cancellation a new booking is accepted again and the sandbox holds exactly 40 confirmed.

**Worth a reviewer's eye**

- When a write is refused I report the overlap (409) ahead of the limit (429) if both hold. AC3 reads that way to me, but it is a judgement call.
- The diagnosis happens after the failed write, so the obstacle can be gone by the time it is read — e.g. the blocking session was cancelled in between. I report 409 `slot_taken` in that case rather than retrying the insert. A retry loop felt like more machinery than this demo wants; say the word if you would rather have one.

Handoff reconciler: the review stage is pending for this agent, but no review run started after the handoff (last run finished 2026-10-14T14:59:49.592Z, no active run, no held lease). Woke the reviewer once. If no review run starts within 3 minutes, a blocker issue will be opened for the accountable person.

## Approved

Reviewed `main..fix/replay-and-limit` (`f62a312`) against all four acceptance criteria. Every one is met, and I verified the write path myself rather than taking the summary's word for it.

**Diff is confined to the work**: `app/src/booking.js` and the new `app/tests/replay-and-limit.test.js`. `git diff main..fix/replay-and-limit -- app/migrations app/src/worker.js app/tests/booking.test.js app/tests/overlap.test.js app/tests/helpers.js` is empty — no schema change, no existing test touched or weakened (AC4). `worker.js:52` already maps `BookingError.status`/`.code` straight through, so 429 `sandbox_full` reaches the client unchanged.

**Test suite, run here**: `cd app && npm test` → **34 pass, 0 fail**. I also checked out `main` into a throwaway worktree, copied the new test file in, and confirmed 3 of its 4 cases fail there (`too_soon` on the late retry, the key-reuse case, and the limit under concurrency) — so the test genuinely pins the defects.

### Evidence per criterion

**AC1 — order of checks.** `createBooking` (`app/src/booking.js:154-165`) is now `validateStructure` → `findByKey` → `checkEligibility`. The structural set in `validateStructure` is exactly the one the ticket names: sandbox, key, duration, offset-bearing instant, 15-minute boundary, time zone (`booking.js:56-69`). The moving rules are isolated in `checkEligibility` (`booking.js:75-79`) and are unreachable on the replay branch because that branch returns at line 161. Probed: a request that is both structurally bad and far too soon still gets `400 bad_duration`, so structural really is first.

**AC2 — replays.** Confirmed by direct probe, not just the suite: a replay 10 days *after* its own start instant returns 200 with the original id; a replay of a cancelled booking returns `200` + `status: cancelled` + `replayed: true` and does not resurrect it, even when the sandbox has since refilled to 40; the same key with `durationMin` changed returns `422 idempotency_key_reused` in a full sandbox after the cutoff (i.e. reuse is diagnosed before both eligibility and the limit).

**AC3 — the limit holds at the write.** The count moved into the same `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE` as the overlap test (`booking.js:117-131`); the pre-insert `SELECT COUNT(*)` is gone. One statement, one write lock, nothing to overtake. The `tick()` in `tests/d1-sqlite.js` yields before every statement, so the interleaving is real and the old code did lose this race. Beyond the supplied 3-racer test I ran:

- 12 concurrent requests for the single remaining place → exactly 1 confirmed, 11 × `429 sandbox_full`, total 40.
- 50 simultaneous requests into an empty sandbox → exactly 40 confirmed, 10 × `429`.
- 3 concurrent replays of an existing key in a *full* sandbox → all 200, no 429 (the replay check at `booking.js:183-184` correctly precedes `refusal`).
- Double-submit of one new key at the limit boundary → `201` + `200`, total 40.
- Overlap in a full sandbox → `409 slot_taken`; overlap in a non-full sandbox → `409`; fresh key in a full sandbox → `429`; one cancellation frees exactly one place and the next request is refused again.
- The count is scoped per sandbox — a full sandbox does not refuse a different one.

I agree with reporting 409 ahead of 429 when both hold; AC3 reads that way to me too.

### One noted behaviour, not blocking

`refusal` (`booking.js:137-148`) diagnoses after the failed write, so a cancellation landing in between makes it misreport. ## Approved — every criterion met, verified independently

Reviewed `1d8db4b..13e6509` on `fix/overlap`. Diff is two files: `app/src/booking.js` (+35/−13) and the new `app/tests/overlap.test.js`. I confirmed `app/migrations/0001_init.sql`, `app/src/worker.js`, `app/src/time.js`, the three pre-existing test files, `app/tests/helpers.js`, `app/tests/d1-sqlite.js`, `app/package.json`, `app/wrangler.toml`, `scripts/` and `.github/workflows/` are byte-for-byte untouched, and the working tree is clean. Nothing unrelated changed; no existing test was weakened or deleted.

### Evidence per criterion

**1. No overlap for any mix of 30/45/60; adjacent still allowed.**
`app/src/booking.js:103-104` uses the half-open predicate `start_utc < :newEnd AND end_utc > :newStart`. I did not take the five seeded cases as proof — I ran my own exhaustive sequential sweep of all 81 combinations (60/45/60 × 30/45/60 × offsets −60…+60 at 15-min steps, the full availability window): the create call was refused with 409 in exactly the cases where the intervals truly intersect, accepted in every other, and no pair of confirmed rows ever overlapped. Adjacency (`end == start`) is accepted, matching the pre-existing `adjacent sessions do not conflict (end is exclusive)` test, which still passes.

**2. The guarantee is at the write, and the rollback is safe.**
The pre-write `start_utc = ?` SELECT is gone (removed at the old `createBooking` clash block); the only gate is now inside the statement that writes — `INSERT … SELECT ? … WHERE NOT EXISTS (…)` in `insertIfFree` (`app/src/booking.js:98-110`), with `meta.changes === 0` as the "interval taken" signal. One SQLite statement runs in its own implicit transaction under the write lock, so there is no read-then-write window left to lose. 300 rounds of 12 mutually overlapping concurrent `createBooking` calls on the real `node:sqlite`-backed D1 stand-in: zero overlapping confirmed rows, every loser a clean `409 slot_taken` (no raw SQL errors leaking), and the confirmed-row count equal to the fulfilled-call count every round — so the winner is never lost either.
Schema diff is empty. `0001_init.sql` is unchanged, which is strictly stronger than backwards compatible: the previous release runs against the identical schema, so the rollback in this release carries no migration risk. The existing index `(sandbox, teacher_id, status, start_utc)` already covers the new range predicate.

**3. Idempotent retry returns the original, also under concurrency.**
Two paths are covered and both are reachable. Same-key retry at the *same* interval: the second insert writes 0 rows (its own row now blocks it), falls to `findByKey` + `sameRequest` at `app/src/booking.js:144-145` and returns 200 replayed. Same-key at a *non-overlapping* interval: the `UNIQUE (sandbox, idem_key)` violation is caught at `:134-137` and mapped to `422 idempotency_key_reused` instead of leaking the constraint error. 300 rounds of 8 concurrent calls sharing one key: always exactly one confirmed row, one booking id, exactly one 201 and seven 200s, zero rejections.

**4. Cancelled sessions never block.**
`status = 'confirmed'` is in the `NOT EXISTS` guard (`app/src/booking.js:103`). 50 rounds of cancel-then-rebook-overlapping across all three durations: every rebook returned 201 and left exactly one confirmed row. The pre-existing `cancellation frees the slot and is idempotent` test still passes.

**5. Tests.**
`cd app && npm test` run by me: **22 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped** (71 ms). The 17 pre-existing tests are all green and unmodified; the 5 new `overlap.test.js` tests cover the reported defect directly.

### One non-blocking note (no change required)

Concurrent same-key misuse where the two requests *overlap* — key `K` for 08:00/60 racing `K` for 08:30/30 — returns `409 slot_taken` rather than the `422 idempotency_key_reused` the sequential path gives, because `written === 0` is reached before the UNIQUE violation can fire (`app/src/booking.js:141-146`). I verified this: non-overlapping gives 422, overlapping gives 409. Both are honest about the outcome, exactly one row is written either way, and no criterion covers it. Worth a line of follow-up only if the API contract wants one status for key reuse regardless of timing.

I agree with the implementer's call to skip the `booking_slots` table: a structural constraint that the rolled-back release would not populate protects nothing after the rollback, and criterion 2 is already satisfied at the write without a migration.

Moving to the approval stage for the operator. Still unpushed and undeployed, as the constraints require.

## Approved

**Evidence per criterion**

1. **Full slot list on both sides, Sydney and Paris times** — met. Each test pins all 7 starts for a 45-minute session as `[UTC instant, Sydney label, Paris label]`:
   - Sat 24 Oct (Sydney date): `05:00Z`–`08:00Z`, Paris 07:00–10:00 (CEST, +2), Sydney 16:00–19:00.

Offsets are asserted directly (Paris 120 → 60, Sydney 660 both days), which is what makes a tzdata or offset regression fail loudly.
2. **Booking the first Monday slot stores the correct instant** — met, and checked at the write, not just the read: the test asserts the presented booking (`2026-10-26T06:00:00.000Z` / `06:45:00.000Z`) **and** then reads `start_utc`/`end_utc` off the stored row via `SELECT … WHERE id = ?`, comparing to `Date.parse(...)`. `06:00Z` is the post-change instant; summer time would have given `05:00Z`. Validation on that path is real too — `withinAvailability` re-derives the Paris wall clock from the instant, so a wrong instant would have been rejected rather than silently stored.
3. **Suite passes, test files only** — met. I ran `cd app && npm test` myself: **26 tests, 26 pass, 0 fail** (77 ms), including the 10 pre-existing booking/overlap/idempotency/cancellation tests and the 6 time tests. `git diff --stat fix/overlap...test/clock-change` → `1 file changed, 98 insertions(+)`. Working tree clean; no remote configured, so nothing was pushed, and no deploy.

**On the flagged expectation change**

The implementer's correction is right, and I verified it against the code rather than the summary. The booking covers `06:00Z`–`06:45Z`; the next start is `06:30Z`–`07:15Z`, and `listSlots` marks a start taken when `b.start_utc < e && b.end_utc > s`, so `06:30Z` overlaps and both come back `taken` while `07:00Z` onward stay free. Two taken / five free is the real behaviour, and the comment in the test explains why — correct to pin that rather than change the app.

**Other things I checked**

- Concurrency and idempotency are untouched by this change; the single-statement `INSERT … WHERE NOT EXISTS` guard and the retry/`UNIQUE` replay paths in `createBooking` still pass their existing tests.
- Each test calls `fresh()` for its own DB and `req()` mints a unique idempotency key, so the new file cannot leak state into or out of the rest of the suite.
- The tests are non-vacuous: `deepEqual` against fixed 7-element arrays fails on any shift in instant, label, or list length — an empty or one-hour-off list cannot pass.

One minor, non-blocking note for later: the assertions depend on the `en-AU` label format (`'Mon, 26 Oct, 17:00'`), so an ICU formatting change in a future Node could break these alongside the existing tests that already use those labels. Not a reason to hold this.

- The count is scoped per sandbox — a full sandbox does not refuse a different one.
